questions.template: Which rock is made from COOLED LAVA or magma?
questions.explain: Igneous rock forms when hot melted rock cools and hardens. Basalt and granite are igneous.

questions.template: Which rock forms in LAYERS, squashed together over ages?
questions.hint: Think of a sandwich pressed for millions of years!
questions.explain: Sediment — sand, mud, tiny shells — settles in layers and gets squashed into sedimentary rock, like sandstone and chalk.

questions.template: Fossils are usually found in which kind of rock?
questions.hint: Fossils need gentle layers to hide in — not fiery lava!
questions.explain: Creatures get buried in soft sediment; as it turns to rock, they become fossils. Lava would burn them up!

questions.template: What is soil mostly made of?
questions.answer: Tiny bits of rock and dead plants
questions.hint: Two ingredients: crumbled rock plus rotted leaves and roots.
questions.explain: Soil is crushed rock mixed with organic matter (dead plants and creatures), air and water — a recipe that takes years!

questions.template: Rock that has been CHANGED by squeezing and heat deep underground is called…?
questions.hint: 'Metamorphosis' means change — like a caterpillar to a butterfly!
questions.explain: Heat and pressure transform old rock into metamorphic rock: limestone becomes marble, mudstone becomes slate.

questions.template: Marble is made when LIMESTONE is heated and squeezed. What kind of rock is marble?
questions.hint: It CHANGED from one rock to another…
questions.explain: Marble is limestone transformed by heat and pressure — a metamorphic makeover. Roman statues thank it!

questions.template: Water soaks THROUGH some rocks. What do we call rocks that let water through?
questions.explain: Permeable rocks like sandstone have tiny gaps that let water through; impermeable rocks like slate block it.

questions.template: What replaces a buried dinosaur's bones to make a fossil?
questions.hint: Rocky stuff dissolved in water, seeping in bit by bit…
questions.explain: Over thousands of years, minerals in water slowly replace the bone, leaving a rock copy — a fossil!

questions.template: Lava cools into igneous rock. That rock wears down into sand, which gets squashed into…?
questions.hint: Layers of squashed bits make which rock family?
questions.explain: Rock keeps changing in a slow loop — the rock cycle! Worn-down bits settle in layers and become sedimentary rock.
